summary: The patch overloads the core `contains_aggregate` property to also report window/over clauses, which is the wrong abstraction (window functions are not aggregates and this property drives GROUP BY/HAVING decisions ORM-wide), and it introduces an operator-precedence bug that crashes on None source expressions. The real fix belongs in the aggregation/subquery-wrapping logic, not here.

issues.description: Operator precedence: `expr and expr.contains_aggregate or expr.contains_over_clause` parses as `(expr and expr.contains_aggregate) or expr.contains_over_clause`. The `expr and` None-guard only protects the first access; when a source expression is None (the very reason the guard exists), `None.contains_over_clause` raises AttributeError. Latent regression for any expression with a None source slot.

Wrong abstraction. `contains_aggregate` is consumed pervasively (GROUP BY construction, HAVING vs WHERE placement, resolve logic). Making it return True for window/over expressions conflates two distinct SQL concepts and risks broadly incorrect SQL generation. The correct fix forces aggregation over window functions into a subquery in the query aggregation logic (get_aggregation), leaving contains_aggregate semantics intact.

Smells like special-casing to make the reported query pass rather than a principled fix; it papers over the symptom by mislabeling window expressions instead of correcting where aggregates-over-windows are emitted to SQL.
No comment explaining why an over-clause check was folded into contains_aggregate, leaving an unexplained and surprising semantic overload.
